items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: I'm a co-writer with Dave Bartholomew.

ctx.x: No, no, he didn't have a contract, a recording contract with him. The recording contract was with this company that, Deluxe. Deluxe. Deluxe. Deluxe. Deluxe said, if Dave don't get his name off the record, they was gonna sue. So, okay. So what I had to do, they said I had to come to New York. Cosmo and I, they were the first, they were not heard of too much. Cosmo and I was the first black, white to get a sleeping bird train from here in New Orleans. And this is true. We talk about this now, me and Cosmo. Nobody…
I think one of these black or white musicians?

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: I went to Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew. And we sat down and I signed all these papers.

ctx.x: So when did Tommy come to you?

When I got in the music business and when I went to record, I went to Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew. And we sat down and I signed all these papers. You know, if I had a hit record I wouldn't have got no money I guess. Same way. But anyway, they discussed a professional name. And so he came up with, he said, well let's think of something. And one name always stick in my mind. He said, let's come with something like Memphis Slim or something. And I listened at him tossing names around and then I said,…
Oh, you mean making it a professional name?
